questions.q: In an Airflow DAG, what does `start_date` actually control?
options: The exact wall-clock time the DAG begins running when deployed
The earliest logical date Airflow is willing to schedule a run for
The date the DAG's code was first written
It has no effect unless `catchup` is also set
questions.explain: `start_date` is the earliest logical date Airflow will schedule a run for, not the moment the DAG starts executing when deployed.

questions.q: Why would a retraining DAG typically set `catchup=False`?
options: To make the DAG run faster
To avoid Airflow backfilling every missed schedule interval between start_date and now the moment the DAG is deployed
Because catchup is required for cron expressions to work
To disable the schedule parameter entirely
questions.explain: With catchup enabled (the default), Airflow backfills every missed interval since start_date. For a daily retrain, that could mean many backdated runs firing at once on first deploy — catchup=False avoids this.

questions.q: How does an Airflow Dataset-triggered DAG differ from a DAG scheduled with a cron expression?
options: It runs more frequently than any cron schedule could
Its schedule is the dataset itself — it runs when an upstream task writes to that outlet, not on a timer
It requires an S3KeySensor to function
There is no functional difference
questions.explain: A DAG scheduled with `schedule=[some_dataset]` runs when the dataset is updated by an upstream task's outlet, rather than on a fixed timer.

questions.q: What is the main drawback of the older sensor pattern (e.g. `S3KeySensor`) that Airflow Datasets address?
options: Sensors cannot check for files in cloud storage
Sensors repeatedly poll a location on a timer to check if something exists, which Datasets avoid via an explicit outlet/trigger relationship
Sensors are faster but less reliable than Datasets
Sensors only work with Kubeflow, not Airflow
questions.explain: Sensors poll repeatedly asking "does this exist yet?" Datasets instead let an upstream task explicitly declare it produced data, triggering the downstream DAG directly without polling.

questions.q: What does `client.create_recurring_run()` do in the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK?
options: Deletes a pipeline run
Schedules a pipeline to run repeatedly according to a cron expression, configured against the KFP backend
Compiles a pipeline into IR YAML
Registers a trained model
questions.explain: `create_recurring_run()` is KFP's mechanism for scheduling a pipeline on a cron-based recurring basis, analogous to Airflow's schedule parameter but configured via the client against the backend.
